Subject: CCPA/CPRA classification + telemetry evidence request

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our security team had two quick asks before we progress to legal:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood would be designated as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA for the BrightPath deployment (we will be sending hashed PHI-derived prompts)?
2) We need a tight summary of telemetry types you collect (logs, tokens, nested telemetry), retention windows, and whether any telemetry is transferred cross-state or used for model training.

If you can point to a short packet or attach the specific DPA exhibit that covers this, that would be most helpful — procurement is on a tight cycle.

Thanks,
Kelly Grant

kelly.grant@brightpathhealth.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Kelly Grant <kelly.grant@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Samir Chopra <samir.chopra@brightpathhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA classification + telemetry evidence request

Hi Kelly — thank you, great questions. Short answer up front: Redwood is comfortable being designated a service provider for the BrightPath Health use case. Below is a concise summary and attached artifacts; happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want line-by-line.

Summary (high level):
- Service Provider designation: yes. We operate under the DPA exhibit (attached) which limits use to performance of the contract and prohibits secondary sale or advertising use.
- Telemetry collected: request/response metadata (timestamp, route, model_id), aggregated runtime metrics (latency, error rates), explicit debug traces only when enabled by customer (opt-in for support). We do not train general models on customer prompt/content without explicit opt-in in contract.
- Retention: production telemetry retained up to 30 days by default, aggregated metrics retained 13 months for platform health/SLAs. Logs related to debugging can be retained up to 90 days when the customer enables support-level logging.
- Cross-state transfers: we may route requests through US-based regions (us-west, us-east) and occasionally through dedicated-host regions for redundancy. No international transfers for BrightPath unless explicitly configured.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-exhibit-v3.pdf (service-provider language + limited use), telemetry-schema-20270219.csv (fields we capture), subprocessor-list-2027-02-19.xlsx (current vendor roster and onshore fallback notes).

Next steps: If procurement/legal want redlines to the DPA exhibit we can accept standard service-provider redlines; any escalations (e.g., requirement to be treated as a controller) will need legal review. Let me know an ETA for review and whether you want security to triage the telemetry schema with our security lead.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 10:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA classification + telemetry evidence request (internal)

Chloe — looped in security and legal as action items. A few operational notes for our reply:

- Confirm explicit clause references in the attached DPA exhibit: call out section 3.2 (limited use), 4.1 (no sale), and paragraph on training prohibition. I will paste the paragraph from the internal template in a follow-up if you want.
- Telemetry: the telemetry-schema CSV is fine but procurement may ask for a small mapping doc that ties each field to purpose (e.g., request_id -> routing/reconciliation; response_tokens -> cost accounting only, hashed before storage). Marissa — can you prepare the mapping doc and mark anything that is PII/PHI?
- Subprocessors: attach the baseline roster and highlight onshore fallbacks (we can commit to an onshore fallback for auth and logging). Make sure the spreadsheet flags SOC2 coverage or equivalent for each vendor.

I can sign off on the short-form answers; if legal wants to add a customer-specific amendment call me out and I’ll prioritize.

-Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Chopra <samir.chopra@brightpathhealth.com>

Cc: Kelly Grant <kelly.grant@brightpathhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightpathhealth.com>, legal@brightpathhealth.com

Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA classification + telemetry evidence request

Chloe — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple clarifying follow-ups before we send to legal:

1) For the "no training" statement: can you add explicit language indicating that any model improvements using BrightPath data would require written consent and a separate amendment? Procurement wants a one-sentence commitment.
2) For telemetry retention: can you confirm whether we can request shorter retention windows (e.g., 7 days for raw logs) as a contract option? If so, note that in the DPA exhibit or propose an addendum we can sign.

We also received the subprocessor roster (thanks) — we flagged two vendors for follow-up (AuthN provider and observability vendor). Can Redwood confirm both vendors are SOC 2 Type II or provide equivalent evidence.

If you can reply with the one-sentence training commitment and a note about configurable retention by EOD PST, that will keep this moving to legal.

Thanks,
Samir Chopra
VP, IT Procurement | BrightPath Health
